rootText: Home Lifestage Settling Down Settling Down Settling down looks different for everyone – you could be getting married, buying a home, or trying for your first child. But one thing’s for certain: you’re planning to safeguard the life you’re creating and its future. Contact us Build your security as you build your new life Consider your priorities for you and your family and make a plan to build a bright future for everyone. High priority Protection In the event of unexpected circumstances such as critical illnesses, accidents, or death, you and your loved ones’ needs and livelihood might be affected. Your priority for protection: Health insurance for hospitalisation.Protection against accidents and major illnesses so that your needs during recovery continue to be met.Financial payout for death, terminal illness, and total and permanent disability.Maternity insurance if you’re planning for children. Plan your protection High priority Wealth You have likely taken on more financial demands such as a wedding, home mortgage, future children’s education, and retirement. Your priority for wealth: Savings for immediate and future expenses.Retirement planning. Build your wealth Learn more about your needs Protection Wealth Protection Safeguarding your health grows in importance as you embark on a new phase of life. Saving for your upcoming milestones will be easier when you don’t have to worry about medical expenses. What you already have¹ If you are a Singaporean or PR, you’re automatically covered by three national schemes: MediSave A national savings scheme which helps CPF members save for future medical expenses, especially during retirement. MediShield Life A health insurance for large hospital bills and selected outpatient treatment costs. CareShield Life Long-term care insurance scheme for financial support and monthly cash payouts in event of severe disability What you may consider² With big-ticket items lined up in your future, being sufficiently protected is critical in ensuring that your savings can be used as intended – for the new life you’re building. National schemes do not fully cover: Hospitalisation An Integrated Shield Plan (IP) provides additional coverage for private hospitals or higher ward classes in public hospitals. Critical Illness You’ll need coverage of 4x annual income. (Recommended)³ Death & Total and Permanent Disability You’ll need coverage of 9 – 10x annual income. (Recommended)³ Savings² To stay covered and accumulate savings over the years. Maternity Coverage for baby and mum. It’s recommended to spend at most 15% of take-home pay on insurance protection. Why act now Health crises can cause income loss and depletion of family funds². Ensure either partner can sustain the family if the other faces an unfortunate event. Connect with a Financial Representative for personalised coverage. Misconceptions? Let’s correct them. Check out some common misunderstandings about financial planning and their truths. Having a plan to grow your money steadily will help achieve your goals including future expenses and retiring comfortably with your partner. Basics – what you should have³ Emergency Funds At least 3 – 6 months’ worth of expenses (including dependants) for rainy days. Legacy Planning A plan for a will, family trusts, life insurance, powers of attorney, and CPF nominations. What you may consider² Creating new memories during your new phase of life will need savings. Giving your money time to grow can mean that your future milestones can be met comfortably. Investment It is recommended to allocate at least 10%3 of your take-home pay for key milestones. A Retirement Plan³ It is never too early to start building your nest egg for the retirement lifestyle you want, including monthly payouts. Why act now Supporting dependants and your lifestyle requires building a well-diversified portfolio². As lifespans are increasing⁴, you’ll need a plan for your financial needs in the future.
